newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes down as pessimism bites.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes down as pessimism bites.

text.p: 1400 GMT - The Czech PX50 closes down on Thursday with dealers blaming pessimism about the economy.
* Overall, 134 shares rise, 145 fall, 72 unchanged. Turnover, 1.0 billion crowns, volume, 883,427 shares.
The Czech PX50 plunged 2.5 percent on Thursday to 490.1 as pessimism about the economy again overshadowed the equities market, dealers said.

Major issues bore the brunt of the declines, with SPT Telecom falling 156 crowns, 5.0 percent, to 2,954 CEZ losing 44 crowns, 4.7 percent, to 901 and Komercni Banka down 162 crowns, 7.8 percent, to 1,913.
"Looking at the longer term it doesn't look that good....If the whole economy is not going to be right how can people think their shares will bring good returns," said Lubos Vystavel of ING Barings.

The Czech government on Thursday elaborated on its latest plan to boost the ailing economy. The new Finance Minister Ivan Pilip said he would make reform of the capital markets a top priority along with stabilisation of the crown.

Deputy Prime Minister Josef Lux added that the government would push through "tens of billions" of crowns in new public spending cuts and said inflation would rise by an extra three to four percentage points because of the recent crisis surrounding the Czech crown.
